title: Refactor XLA Profiler to be Framework-Agnostic via Shared C-State
body:
Refactor XLA Profiler to be Framework-Agnostic via Shared C-State

This CL refactors the XLA profiler to eliminate its direct C++ dependency on TensorFlow's Python modules. This change resolves deadlocks that occurred in non-TensorFlow environments (e.g., JAX-only) and creates a more robust, high-performance, and architecturally clean solution.

## Problem
Previously, the C++ PythonHookContext would directly import the tensorflow.python.profiler.trace Python module to set an enabled flag. This operation was performed while the C++ thread already held Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL).

This caused several critical issues:

* GIL Deadlocks: If the import failed (e.g., because TensorFlow was not installed), pybind11's exception handler would attempt to re-acquire the GIL. This caused the thread to deadlock by waiting for a lock it already held.
* Fragile Architecture: This made the profiler fragile and unusable outside of a full TensorFlow environment, affecting JAX-only users.
* Tight Coupling: It created an architecturally unsound dependency from a low-level C++ library to a high-level Python module.

## Solution
This change decouples the C++ profiler from Python's module structure by using a shared C++ memory location as the single source of truth for the profiler's state.

1. Shared C++ State (traceme_state):

    * A new, minimal cc_library     (//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/python/profiler/internal:traceme_state) is introduced.
    * It owns a global std::atomic<bool> that serves as the definitive "TraceMe enabled" state.
    * The C++ PythonHookContext now writes directly to this C++ variable, removing all Python module interactions.

2. High-Performance Python Access via ctypes:

   * The _pywrap_traceme pybind extension is updated with a get_traceme_enabled_addr() function that returns the raw memory address of the C++ atomic boolean.
   * In Python, trace.py calls this function once on import and uses the ctypes library to create a direct pointer to this memory address.
This allows Python code to check the trace.enabled status with the performance of a direct memory read, completely avoiding any pybind function call overhead.

## Benefits
* Fixes Deadlocks: By removing the cross-language import, the GIL deadlock issue is completely resolved.
* Decouples Code: The profiler's C++ core is now truly framework-agnostic.
High Performance: The critical trace.enabled check in Python remains a fast, overhead-free memory access.
* Clean Architecture: The dependency is now unidirectional and logical—Python reads from a C++ utility, not the other way around.

title: Fix configure.py sysconfig fallback used for Python library path detection
body:
### Summary
`configure.py:get_python_path()` probes Python’s site-packages via a `python -c` snippet using `site.getsitepackages()`. When that probe fails, it falls back to a `sysconfig.get_path("purelib")` snippet.

The fallback snippet was missing a closing `)`, causing the `python -c` call to raise a `SyntaxError` and potentially breaking `./configure` on environments where the fallback path is exercised.

### Changes
- Fix the sysconfig fallback `python -c` snippet in `configure.py`.
- Add a regression test that forces the `site.getsitepackages()` probe to fail and asserts the corrected sysconfig fallback snippet is used.

### Testing
- `python3 -m unittest -v configure_test`

### Notes
- Only the fallback command string is changed; the common `site.getsitepackages()` path is unchanged.

title: Upgrade GitHub Actions to latest versions
body:
## Summary

Upgrade GitHub Actions to their latest versions for improved features, bug fixes, and security updates.

## Changes

| Action | Old Version(s) | New Version | Release | Files |
|--------|---------------|-------------|---------|-------|
| `peter-evans/create-pull-request` | [`84ae59a`](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request/commit/84ae59a2cdc2258d6fa0732dd66352dddae2a412) | [`98357b1`](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request/commit/98357b18bf14b5342f975ff684046ec3b2a07725) | [Release](https://github.com/peter-evans/create-pull-request/releases/tag/v8) | release-branch-cherrypick.yml, update-rbe.yml |

## Why upgrade?

Keeping GitHub Actions up to date ensures:
- **Security**: Latest security patches and fixes
- **Features**: Access to new functionality and improvements
- **Compatibility**: Better support for current GitHub features
- **Performance**: Optimizations and efficiency improvements

### Security Note

Actions that were previously pinned to commit SHAs remain pinned to SHAs (updated to the latest release SHA) to maintain the security benefits of immutable references.

### Testing

These changes only affect CI/CD workflow configurations and should not impact application functionality. The workflows should be tested by running them on a branch before merging.

title: Warn users about GPU support on Windows
body:
### Summary
Adds a one-time runtime warning for TensorFlow >= 2.11 on native Windows
to clarify that GPU support is not available, even if CUDA/cuDNN are installed.

### Motivation
Many Windows users believe their GPU setup is broken when
`tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU")` returns an empty list.
This change provides an explicit warning explaining the platform limitation.

Fixes #106684

### Behavior
- No behavior change in device discovery
- Warning is emitted once per process
- No new dependencies introduced

title: Fix TFL to TOSA constant truncation to i48 that broke tosa.greater legalization
body:
- removed the legacy code path that truncated every 64-bit TFLite constant down to 48 bits, which produced `tosa.greater` ops whose operands having mismatched integer widths violating the TOSA spec.

- updated the broadcast-to tests so their CHECK lines now expect i64 constants, as legalization now preserves the original element types all the way through.

title: Fix dynamic batch handling for TFL FullyConnected in TOSA legalization
body:
Fixing TFLite to TOSA legalization of `tfl.fully_connected` when the batch dimension is dynamic.

- The previous code always divided `input_type.getNumElements()` by the filter depth, which returns `0` for partially dynamic tensors, producing reshape shapes like `[0, 512]` and finally a `tosa.reshape` with a 0-sized batch

- To fix this I am adding a guard the batch computation so that dynamic inputs keep `ShapedType::kDynamic`, allowing the pattern to respect dynamic batch sizes reported in #104313

- Also adding `test_fullyconnected_dynamic_batch` test to `tfl-to-tosa-pipeline.mlir`, checking the generated `tosa.const_shape` ops and reshape flow to prevent regressions.

Fixes #104313

title: Make filecheck prefixes a parameter.
body:
Make filecheck prefixes a parameter.

`CHECK-PTX` and `CHECK-GCN` have been considered valid prefixes only if the build is configured as a ROCM or a CUDA build. This change makes this a parameter to the RunFilecheck functions and allows individual tests to decide which prefixes they wanna use.

title: [XLA:GPU] Fix bugs when sorting two elements with a fused iota.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Fix bugs when sorting two elements with a fused iota.

The first bug was that we did not pass the right HloInstruction to EmitIota().
The second bug happens if the comparison determines that the two elements don't
have to be swapped. Then we would not write the computed iota into the output
buffer, as we only write elements if they need to be swapped.

title: [XLA:GPU] Add xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 flag to XLA.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Add xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 flag to XLA.

This flag allows using the dot precision algorithm ALG_DOT_BF16_BF16_F32 for f32 dot ops by default on GPU, which can improve performance at the expense of numerical accuracy.

This change just adds the flag, the implementation will follow.
